source.title: Robustness of Accuracy Metric and its Inspirations in Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Pengfei Chen; Jun-Jie Ye; Guang-Yong Chen; Jingwei Zhao; Pheng-Ann Heng

record.tranche_reason: The study tests learning under class-conditional label noise, but does not apply fully random labels or the original random-label intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for partially corrupted labels and discusses cited work on random-label fitting. It does not test completely random labels, unstructured inputs, or the other listed interventions.
record.test_reason: The study bears on V4 through its own noise-rate experiments and its analysis and experiments showing that perfect noisy-label training fit depends on sample size relative to model capacity. Completely random labels are not required to test these parts of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Under diagonally dominant class-conditional noise and the stated realizability assumptions, maximizing population noisy accuracy also maximizes clean accuracy. With sufficiently many samples relative to hypothesis-class complexity, maximizing empirical noisy accuracy can yield an approximately optimal classifier. The authors also theoretically justify noisy validation and demonstrate its practical utility through NTS.
record.recipe_differences: Experiments use partially corrupted class-conditional labels and noisy-label training methods; they do not reproduce the fully random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Training sample count changes the reported train/test accuracy characterizations; the authors also note that strong augmentation can underfit in a rare setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Noisy validation selects useful teachers, and teacher-derived student labels often improve test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy validation can support model selection and distillation under suitable class-conditional noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Early-selected cross-entropy teachers outperform final teachers; the authors interpret later deterioration through previously reported memorization effects.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early stopping can improve clean test accuracy during noisy-label training.

record.problems: The experiments use partially corrupted labels rather than fully random labels; some characterization results are shown in figures, while the numerical examples do not test the listed random-label claim versions directly.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the reported outcomes concern class-conditional label noise and noisy-validation selection, not the specified random-label behaviors. Figure 3 and Tables 1–3 report related noisy-label results; random-label fitting is mentioned as cited prior work.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, chance test performance, and fitting with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs.
A corruption sweep spanning none to all, chance performance at complete corruption, and simultaneous verification of perfect training fit throughout that sweep.
Random-label fitting with explicit regularization and clean-label generalization after removing regularization.
Direct measurement of when real patterns and individual noisy labels are learned. Early versus final test accuracy does not establish this ordering.

missing.what: V4-linked final-epoch CE test accuracies across uniform corruption rates, retaining dataset, noise rate, uncertainty, and augmentation conditions. Although rows_left_out mentions Table 1, its dismissal of these results as irrelevant overlooks the tested degradation component.

Paired noisy-training and clean-test accuracies for the fixed MLP across sample sizes, including clean oracles. Although rows_left_out mentions Figure 3, these results qualify the perfect-fit component and should be retained.

record.verdict_notes: The population accuracy ceiling of 1−ε is distinct from finite-sample memorization. Neither that ceiling nor the small-MLP experiments refutes random-label fitting by sufficiently expressive networks. NTS performance and augmentation ablations do not establish V1 or V5.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling of the training set, chance test error, and fitting without changes to architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training-time cost relative to true labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
The experiments vary class-conditional noise and report train/test accuracy, but do not sweep random corruption from none to all while establishing perfect training fit throughout.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels, and whether their removal harms generalization on true labels.
Whether true patterns are learned before noisy labels are memorized.

relationships.condition: Final-epoch cross-entropy teachers on CIFAR-10/100 with uniform corruption rates 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6; test-degradation component only.
relationships.reason: From Table 1, rather than extracted rows: test accuracy decreases monotonically, 86.30→74.18→59.15% on CIFAR-10 and 70.61→55.96→38.25% on CIFAR-100. Training fit is not established.
relationships.display_finding: Final-epoch test accuracy declined successively from 86.30% to 74.18% to 59.15% on CIFAR-10 and from 70.61% to 55.96% to 38.25% on CIFAR-100.

relationships.condition: Fixed two-hidden-layer MLP on circles and moons as training sample count increases under fixed class-conditional noise.
relationships.reason: From Figure 3 and Section 5.1, rather than extracted rows: at 100 samples train/test accuracies are 0.99/0.76 and 0.96/0.73; at 1,000 they are 0.75/0.96 for both datasets. Perfect noisy-label fit depends on sample size relative to capacity.
relationships.display_finding: At 100 samples, training/test accuracies were 0.99/0.76 for circles and 0.96/0.73 for moons; at 1,000 samples, both reached 0.75/0.96.

tranche.reason: Own experiments test noisy-label training fit and generalization through sample-size variation and partial class-conditional corruption, using a different protocol from completely random labeling.

source_check.notes: No result rows were supplied; verdicts are supported directly by Table 1 and Figure 3. Completely random labels, perfect CIFAR training fit, and a full corruption sweep from none to all are untested.
